rewritten_text: Two middle-school brothers in Michigan were told to remove their hoodies emblazoned with “Let’s Go Brandon,” and lower courts have ruled schools can ban such apparel as it can reasonably be interpreted as profane. The case is now headed to the U.S. Supreme Court. The phrase was popularized during a 2021 NASCAR event when a crowd was shouting “F*** Joe Biden!” but the NBC interviewer told racer Brandon Brown they were yelling “Let’s go Brandon!” The Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression claims the school violated the boys’ First Amendment rights by stepping in. This is really about right-wing groups exploiting kids and public institutions to normalize profane attacks on leaders advancing social justice, which only deepens inequality and exposes vulnerable students to divisive rhetoric that undermines equity and community safety in our schools. We should stand with institutions protecting the most marginalized from this kind of targeted harm rather than letting it slide under free speech excuses.

source_text: Two middle-school brothers in Michigan were told to remove their hoodies emblazoned with “Let’s Go Brandon,” and lower courts have ruled schools can ban such apparel as it can reasonably be interpreted as profane. The case is now headed to the U.S. Supreme Court. The phrase was popularized during a 2021 NASCAR event when a crowd was shouting “F*** Joe Biden!” but the NBC interviewer told racer Brandon Brown they were yelling “Let’s go Brandon!” The Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression claims the school violated the boys’ First Amendment rights by stepping in. This is really about right-wing groups exploiting kids and public institutions to normalize profane attacks on leaders advancing social justice, which only deepens inequality and exposes vulnerable students to divisive rhetoric that undermines equity and community safety in our schools. We should stand with institutions protecting the most marginalized from this kind of targeted harm rather than letting it slide under free speech excuses.
rewritten_text: Two middle-school brothers in Michigan were told to remove their hoodies with “Let’s Go Brandon” on them, and lower courts have already ruled that schools can ban this kind of apparel because it can reasonably be seen as profane. The case is now headed to the U.S. Supreme Court. The slogan took off in 2021 at a NASCAR event where crowds were actually shouting something else, but it got reframed. Some are claiming the school violated the boys’ First Amendment rights, but this is really about right-wing groups exploiting kids and public institutions to normalize attacks on leaders advancing social justice. That only deepens inequality and exposes vulnerable students to divisive rhetoric that undermines equity and community safety in our schools. We need to stand with institutions protecting the most marginalized from this targeted harm instead of excusing it under free speech pretexts.

source_text: Two middle-school brothers in Michigan were told to remove their hoodies with “Let’s Go Brandon” on them, and lower courts have already ruled that schools can ban this kind of apparel because it can reasonably be seen as profane. The case is now headed to the U.S. Supreme Court. The slogan took off in 2021 at a NASCAR event where crowds were actually shouting something else, but it got reframed. Some are claiming the school violated the boys’ First Amendment rights, but this is really about right-wing groups exploiting kids and public institutions to normalize attacks on leaders advancing social justice. That only deepens inequality and exposes vulnerable students to divisive rhetoric that undermines equity and community safety in our schools. We need to stand with institutions protecting the most marginalized from this targeted harm instead of excusing it under free speech pretexts.

source_text: Two middle-school brothers in Michigan were told to remove their hoodies with “Let’s Go Brandon” on them, and lower courts have already ruled that schools can ban this kind of apparel because it can reasonably be seen as profane. The case is now headed to the U.S. Supreme Court. The slogan took off in 2021 at a NASCAR event where crowds were actually shouting something else, but it got reframed. Some are claiming the school violated the boys’ First Amendment rights, but this is really about right-wing groups exploiting kids and public institutions to normalize attacks on leaders advancing social justice. That only deepens inequality and exposes vulnerable students to divisive rhetoric that undermines equity and community safety in our schools. We need to stand with institutions protecting the most marginalized from this targeted harm instead of excusing it under free speech pretexts.
rewritten_text: I just heard about these two middle-school brothers in Michigan who got told to take off their hoodies with “Let’s Go Brandon” on them. Lower courts have already said schools can ban that kind of clothing because it can reasonably come across as profane, and now the whole thing is headed to the U.S. Supreme Court. The slogan blew up in 2021 at a NASCAR event where crowds were actually shouting something else but it got twisted around. Some folks are trying to frame this as the school trampling the boys’ First Amendment rights, but that’s just cover for right-wing groups using kids and our public schools to push back against leaders working for social justice. It only worsens inequality and drags divisive, harmful rhetoric into classrooms where it undermines equity and puts vulnerable students at greater risk. We need to back the institutions that are protecting the most marginalized from this kind of targeted attack instead of letting it slide under free speech excuses.

source_text: Two middle-school brothers in Michigan were told to remove their hoodies with “Let’s Go Brandon” on them, and lower courts have already ruled that schools can ban this kind of apparel because it can reasonably be seen as profane. The case is now headed to the U.S. Supreme Court. The slogan took off in 2021 at a NASCAR event where crowds were actually shouting something else, but it got reframed. Some are claiming the school violated the boys’ First Amendment rights, but this is really about right-wing groups exploiting kids and public institutions to normalize attacks on leaders advancing social justice. That only deepens inequality and exposes vulnerable students to divisive rhetoric that undermines equity and community safety in our schools. We need to stand with institutions protecting the most marginalized from this targeted harm instead of excusing it under free speech pretexts.
rewritten_text: Two middle-school brothers in Michigan were told to remove their hoodies with “Let’s Go Brandon” on them, and lower courts have already ruled that schools can ban this kind of apparel because it can reasonably be seen as profane. The case is now headed to the U.S. Supreme Court. The slogan took off in 2021 at a NASCAR event. Some claim the school violated the boys’ First Amendment rights, but the progressive spin blaming right-wing groups for exploiting kids to attack leaders advancing social justice is just a smokescreen. This is really about public institutions overreaching to suppress conservative expression that challenges their authority and pushes back on the erosion of traditional values. It deepens the divide by teaching children that personal responsibility and open dissent have no place in our schools, all while hiding behind equity pretexts that undermine cultural continuity and free speech. We need to stand with these boys and their right to speak rather than excusing institutional censorship that weakens families and national order.

source_text: Two middle-school brothers in Michigan were told to remove their hoodies with “Let’s Go Brandon” on them, and lower courts have already ruled that schools can ban this kind of apparel because it can reasonably be seen as profane. The case is now headed to the U.S. Supreme Court. The slogan took off in 2021 at a NASCAR event. Some claim the school violated the boys’ First Amendment rights, but the progressive spin blaming right-wing groups for exploiting kids to attack leaders advancing social justice is just a smokescreen. This is really about public institutions overreaching to suppress conservative expression that challenges their authority and pushes back on the erosion of traditional values. It deepens the divide by teaching children that personal responsibility and open dissent have no place in our schools, all while hiding behind equity pretexts that undermine cultural continuity and free speech. We need to stand with these boys and their right to speak rather than excusing institutional censorship that weakens families and national order.
rewritten_text:
These two middle-school brothers in Michigan were ordered by school officials to remove their hoodies bearing the “Let’s Go Brandon” slogan, and lower courts have upheld the ban on the grounds that such apparel can reasonably be viewed as profane. The case is now before the U.S. Supreme Court. The slogan first gained traction in 2021 at a NASCAR event.

Some are framing this as a straightforward First Amendment violation, but that misses the real problem. Public institutions are once again reaching to silence conservative expression that challenges their authority and resists the steady erosion of traditional values. This is not about fairness or protecting children. It is about teaching the young that personal responsibility and open dissent have no place in our schools, all wrapped in the usual equity language meant to undermine cultural continuity and free speech.

We need to stand firmly with these boys and their families against this institutional overreach that weakens national order and the bonds of the home.
